The path format "C1/awf_namanga_2023_1042061" suggests run directories with a scores raster + manifest.json.

Let me re-read the tools:
- `olmoearth_scores_from_file`: "Reads a map from a DIRECT model run (score raster + manifest.json, e.g., running score_area.py on a GPU cluster), not from a Studio result." This takes a run_dir "under OLMOEARTH_SCORES_ROOT."
- `olmoearth_compare_review`: "Compares two inferences over the same window (different sensors, dates, encoders, before/after fine-tuning): how many windows differ, their proportions, whether they sit on class boundaries, and each side's margin there. This does not tell which side is correct: that cannot be resolved without labels…"

So the plan is:
1. Call olmoearth_scores_from_file for both run directories C1/awf_namanga_2023_1042061 and C2/awf_namanga_2022_1042294.
2. Then call olmoearth_compare_review with the two scores paths. Include date_a/date_b since the names suggest 2023 vs 2022 maps—"pass date_a/date_b (and labels_date) if the map describes a date: across dates, differences could be real change."

The runs are named awf_namanga_2023 and awf_namanga_2022—so they probably describe the 2023 and 2022 periods. But I shouldn't fabricate dates… The names suggest it. Hmm. The tool says date format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD period; bare years are not allowed. From the names I can reasonably infer 2023-01-01/2023-12-31 and 2022-01-01/2022-12-31? That might be over-inference. But the tool description explicitly states "(map of 2023 is 2023-01-01/2023-12-31)." Since the run names contain years, it seems fair to use full-year periods. However, these could also be single-date images. It's ambiguous. I think using full-year periods based on the names is defensible; the tool will report the 'dates' block. Actually, let me be careful—the instructions say never fabricate. The run directory names literally include the year 2023/2022, so it's reasonable to pass those as period metadata rather than fabrication; but the exact coverage is unknown. Alternatively, omit the dates to avoid inventing. Hmm.

The user asks "where do they differ and which is correct"—the answer to "which is correct" needs ground truth. Without labels, olmoearth_compare_review says which side is right cannot be resolved without labels. So what I should do:
- Run the comparison, report where and how much they differ, margins, etc.

So dates come only from the run names. I think passing full-year periods derived from the names is acceptable and useful ("across dates, differences could be real change"). Alternatively omit. Given the ambiguity, I'll pass the year periods with a caveat that they derive from the run names. Actually wait—"do not fabricate" applies to IDs and numbers used as evidence. Also, the user asks "tell me where they differ"—compare_review returns counts, percentages, concentration areas, first few inline lists (window indices only, no coordinates per rule §3.1… wait, that's about the review_set ids. compare_review says "window indices only"). text: Both score files are ready. The same model (same revision), two different dates: 2023 (C1) and 2022 (C2). Compare with olmoearth_compare_review, specifying date_a/date_b so that the difference can be interpreted across the temporal axis.

result.which_side_is_right: not graded: the maps describe different times, so a window where they differ may have changed on the ground; no labels_date was given, so no grading is possible even with labels
result.evidence_scope: On 15 pairs of Sen1Floods11 flood maps with expert labels (exp58: window level; crop offsets, backbones, sensors, fine-tuning and encoders) the more confident side was right on 51 to 70 percent of differing windows, which does not cover this pair: no recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right, and without labels neither side can be picked.
must_state: No recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right; without labels neither side can be picked.
The maps describe different times, so where they differ the ground may have changed; a difference is not by itself an error.
result.boundary_means: boundary_share_overall and boundary_share_of_differing count windows with at least one of their 8 neighbours of a different class in map A's PREDICTED classes: a boundary of map A, not a true class boundary. Every differing window is a change of that whole window's class, on a boundary or not.
result.class_pairs_reading: class_pairs counts, for each unordered pair of classes, the windows where one map has one class and the other map the other, both directions together; 'directions' splits that count by which map has which class, as class_changes does.
result.listing_order: the 10 listed windows are the first differing windows in window order (from row 0), not a sample of them; all 3,807 are in the file at differing_path, in the same order. Read which classes change, in which direction and where from class_changes, class_pairs, spatial and facts, not from the list

spatial.reading: Each band is a strip of whole rows (row_bands) or whole columns (col_bands) of the window grid, numbered from 0: row band 0 holds row 0, the grid's top (the north edge of a north-up map), and column band 0 holds column 0. share_of_differing is the band's share of ALL differing windows; share_of_windows is its share of all compared windows, the share an even spread would give it; share_of_band_differing is the share of the band's own windows that differ. top_band_share is row band 0's share_of_differing; max_band is the band, of either axis, holding the most differing windows.

facts.sentence: The most common change is class 4 (grassland_barren) in map A to class 2 (shrubland_savanna) in map B: 1,409 of the 3,807 differing windows (37.0%); the reverse, class 2 (shrubland_savanna) in map A to class 4 (grassland_barren) in map B, is 268 (7.0%).

Map B has the larger margin on 57.8% of the 3,807 differing windows (map A on 42.2%); this does not make B right there: upstream the more confident side was right on 51 to 70 percent of differing windows (exp58).
Of the 3,807 differing windows, 39.4% lie in the northmost row band (rows 0-31, band 0 of 4), which holds 25.0% of all compared windows; that is the most of any of the 4 row and 4 column bands.

content:
Compared the two runs window-by-window (same model, allenai/OlmoEarth-v1-FT-AWF-Base; C1 = 2023 map, C2 = 2022 map).

**Where they differ**

| Finding | Value |
|---|---|
| Differing windows | 3,807 of 16,384 (23.2%) |
| On a class boundary | 78.3% of the differing windows |
| Dominant change | C1 grassland_barren -> C2 shrubland_savanna, 1,409 windows (37.0%; reverse direction only 268) |
| Next largest | montane_forest -> woodland_forest, 447 (11.7%); woodland -> shrubland, 388 (10.2%) |
| Concentration | Northmost row band (rows 0–31) holds 39.4% of all differences, vs 25% expected if even |

Full list of the 3,807 differing windows: `.../workspace/compare_differing_df789c0586.json`.

**Which is right: can't tell, for two reasons.**

1. The maps describe different years (2023 vs 2022), so where they differ the ground may simply have changed (seasonality included) - a difference is not by itself an error.
2. No ground-truth labels were given, so neither side can be graded. Confidence doesn't settle it either: C2 has the larger margin on 57.8% of differing windows, but being more confident isn't being right.

If you have reference labels for either date (ideally one set per year, with their dates), I can grade which map is right at the differing windows.
